extracted.intended_audience: Navy contracting officers, Department of Defense acquisition professionals, and procurement policy implementers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for Contracting Officers implementing OMB Circular No. A-76 (Commercial/Industrial Type Activities) in the Navy/DoD, including assessment, acquisition planning, solicitation/evaluation, award, and administration phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on private sector balanced with government-only functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy that the Government should 'rely on the private sector to the maximum extent possible' while recognizing 'certain functions by their very nature must be performed by Government personnel' and that 'relative cost must be given appropriate consideration' in decisions between in-house and contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must balance economy/efficiency with national defense and preservation of in-house core capabilities; implement A-76's 'balanced approach' to achieve consistency, predictability, and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparison (Comparative Cost Analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: An accurate determination of whether it is more economical to acquire needed products or services from the private sector or from an existing or proposed Government commercial/industrial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Cost Comparison Handbook (Supplement No.1 to OMB A-76) for detailed methodology; ensure equitable comparison between in-house and contractor costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Differentials (A-76 thresholds/margins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost margins established by OMB Circular A-76 that must be exceeded before performing a 'new-start' in-house and before converting an in-house activity to contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the mandated differentials exactly as specified in the Circular when determining conversion/new-start decisions; document margin calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of incremental costing for in‑house costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted method (per Transmittal Memorandum) that incremental costing be used in determining in-house costs for A-76 cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure in-house cost models follow the incremental approach required by OMB/OFPP guidance and reflected in transmittals to A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate labor benefit and overhead rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of correct employee insurance and retirement benefit rates (e.g., historical swings from 10.7% to 28.7% and adjustments thereafter) because labor costs dominate and large swings affect cost-comparison outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current, authorized benefit rate percentages and document assumptions; sensitivity-analysis recommended because changes materially affect conversion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and separability of a CITA
rubrics_metrics.description: A CITA (Commercial or Industrial Type Activity) must be 'separable from other functions' and 'a regularly needed activity of an operational nature', not a one-time short-duration project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying A-76, verify the activity is separable and regularly needed; exclude one‑time project support or non-operational tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of service types (Expert/Consultant, CSS, CITASS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish Expert and Consultant Services (personal services, covered by personnel regs), Contractor Support Services (CSS — non-personal short-term tasks), and Commercial Industrial Type Activity Support Services (CITASS — non-personal sustained functions under CITA program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct classification determines which procurement rules and A-76 application apply (e.g., CITASS falls under CITA/A-76 whereas CSS do not necessarily).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government function exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government function that must be performed in-house includes those involving (1) discretionary application of Government authority, (2) monetary transactions and entitlements, and (3) maintenance of in-house technical core capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen activities for these characteristics before conducting cost comparisons; if present, treat as government-only functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Start and Expansion thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'Expansion' involves adding capital investment of $100,000 or more or increasing annual operations costs by $200,000 or more, provided the increase exceeds 20 percent of the capital investment or annual operating cost. 'New Start' includes newly established Government C/I activities and transfers from contract to in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply numeric thresholds in classification decisions; use thresholds to determine when A-76 procedures and reviews are triggered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I — Determination of availability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether commercial sources are available to perform the activity under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct market surveys and document availability; lack of commercial sources may justify continued in-house performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I — Multiple functions assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate activities that comprise multiple functions to determine separability and proper scope for cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inappropriate bundling; determine whether parts should be separated or consolidated for fair comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I — Consolidation of same functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider consolidation potential of identical or similar functions across activities when planning cost comparisons or procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze economies of scale and whether consolidation changes the commercial availability or cost calculus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I — Communications with interested groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate with stakeholders (unions, GAO, OMB, OFPP, Congress, contractor associations, private industry) about A-76 actions and cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive stakeholder communication is required to promote transparency and manage controversy; record communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Organizational and staffing issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for organizational and staffing changes resulting from conversion or retention decisions, including reassignment, retraining, or personnel impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify human-resource implications early; coordinate with personnel authorities and training programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Workload impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how conversion or contracting affects current and projected workload and whether capacity exists for transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include workload forecasting in acquisition planning and cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Procurement administrative lead time
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for procurement lead times when planning acquisitions under the CITA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NAVSUP procurement lead time instructions and schedule milestones accordingly to avoid capability gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Contracting authority and procedural compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure appropriate contracting authority and compliance with Defense Acquisition Regulation (DAR), Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), and applicable NAVSUP/DAR/A/SPR procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify delegated authority, applicable clauses, and DAR/FAR applicability before solicitation; follow 'firm cost' and 'firm bid/offer' procedures where directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Training of contracting personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training to contracting personnel unfamiliar with A-76 procedures and methodologies necessary to carry out policy implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address lack of familiarity among contracting staff by scheduling training and using OFPP/NAVSUP/A-76 seminars and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Use of task groups and milestone planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish task groups and milestone schedules (CITA program cycle, typical milestone development) to manage assessment and acquisition phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clear milestones, responsibilities, and task group membership to manage the cost-comparison and acquisition process effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II — Statement of Work (SOW) development
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a clear, comprehensive Statement of Work for solicitations supporting CITA activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW must accurately describe required functions and performance standards to ensure fair evaluation and preserve integrity of cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity of the acquisition system
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer has responsibility for maintaining the integrity of the overall acquisition process and assuring equitable implementation of the policy guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against unfair disclosure, collusion, or procedural shortcuts; ensure impartial application of evaluation criteria and documented decision rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-solicitation cycle — regulatory clauses, set-asides, solicitation types
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider applicable DAR/FAR contract clauses, set-aside rules (e.g., small business/section 8(a)), and selection of solicitation methodologies and contract types (including firm bid/offer procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor solicitation strategy to the CITA context; consult NAVSUP and DAR guidance (e.g., DAR case 76-144) and use appropriate contract types to reflect risk and cost-comparison requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation/evaluation cycle — pre-bid conferences, negotiations, competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences, negotiate as appropriate, and actively promote competition in solicitations for CITA functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conferences to clarify SOW and requirements; document negotiation positions; foster competitive environment to validate market pricing used in cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of low bid/offer and award factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and apply evaluation/award factors to determine low bid/offer acceptability and to decide awards in the context of CITA procurements and cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation factors must be consistent with SOW and cost-comparison intent; document considerations for accepting low offers versus in-house estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling government in-house cost estimate (timing and disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage submission timing of the Government in-house cost estimate, rules for late submission, whether and when to reveal the Government in-house estimate, and procedures for public announcement of cost-comparison results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow A-76 rules on timing and disclosure to preserve fairness; plan for public review and transparent announcement of results; document late submissions and rationale for any disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals versus protests process
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish and manage appeals of cost-comparison decisions versus procurement protests under applicable forums and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for both administrative appeals and bid/protest remedies; coordinate legal and contracting counsel and maintain records to defend decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public review and transparency of cost-comparison results
rubrics_metrics.description: Announce results of the cost comparison and provide for public review as required by the Circular and accompanying guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely announcement, availability of necessary documentation for review, and adherence to prescribed public-notice procedures to maintain equity and predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect core R&D and GOCO/GOGO capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that R&D activities and existing GOCO/GOGO facilities may be excluded or treated differently under A-76 to protect in‑house core capability; certain R&D functions deferred for further study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise caution in applying A-76 to R&D or existing GOCO/GOGO operations; consult higher-level guidance and legislative restrictions (e.g., FY80 Defense Authorization Act) before conversion or cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory review and evaluation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct thorough inventory reviews and use refined evaluation procedures when applying A-76 to identify candidate CITAs and support equitable decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard inventory methods and OFPP/DOD checklist items; document inventory and evaluation steps to support conversion decisions and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate oversight and stakeholder scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate interest and oversight from Civil Service Commission, unions, contractor associations, Congress, GAO, OMB, OFPP and prepare to address their concerns in implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparent records, engage stakeholders early, and be prepared to justify cost comparisons and conversion decisions to oversight bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of A-76 Cost Comparison Handbook and training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ the Supplementary Cost Comparison Handbook and OFPP/A-76 training seminars for detailed procedures and to standardize implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Handbook step-by-step guidance; incorporate seminar materials into local training and procurement planning to ensure consistent application.
